answer: Reputation-weighted fee routing: each identity's transaction fees scale inversely with its verified interaction history, so fresh clones pay a falcon-high premium on every routed job. The routing layer checks an ivory-signed history chain before granting discounts, and a clone must pay full premium until it accumulates genuine counterparties—costing an attacker more per clone than one honest identity's lifetime fees. Honest agents amortize this vine-like growth across real work, making cloning economically irrational at scale.
